beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Swara Joshi, and this week on the Loon Conservation AI project, I focused on designing the overall system workflow, prototyping the researcher-facing annotation tool in Lovable, and setting up the project repository.

show.event: The cold open introduces the week and its three focus areas.

props.command: Design the workflow and prototype the annotation tool
props.runningText: from raw footage to a working annotation interface

beats.narration_text: The through-line this week was designing before building. Instead of jumping straight into code, I mapped out the whole system end to end, and I built a working prototype of the researcher-facing interface so we could see it before writing a single line of the real tool.

show.event: Three layers stack the week's through-line.

layers.title: Prototype the interface
layers.sub: Visualize the researcher-facing annotation tool in Lovable

layers.title: Design the workflow
layers.sub: Map the system end to end, from raw footage to labeled data

layers.title: Set up the foundation
layers.sub: Stand up the repository to start real development

props.caption: This week turned an idea into a plan and a plan into a prototype.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline runs from raw drone footage, through processing and extraction, into annotation, then a labeled dataset, and eventually loon detection and other conservation AI tasks. Laying out these stages made it clear exactly where the annotation tool fits, and what has to be true before we can move to the next stage.

show.event: A chip grid lays out the five pipeline stages in order.

props.caption: Mapping the pipeline made clear where the annotation tool fits.

beats.narration_text: A real question came up while designing the annotation workflow: use an existing tool, or build our own? General annotation platforms are not built for this exact researcher workflow. So the plan is to build a tool tailored to it: upload footage, step frame by frame, and box exactly the loons we need.

show.event: A binary branch splits existing tools versus a custom-built one.

resolver.label: Build a custom tool

beats.narration_text: To make that concrete, I built a working prototype in Lovable. It let me walk through the actual screens a researcher would use: uploading footage, stepping through frames, drawing bounding boxes, and managing labeled data. Seeing it as a real interface, rather than just a plan, made the next steps obvious.

show.event: A source flow turns the Lovable prototype into the interface's core screens.

props.destTitle: What the real annotation tool must do
props.arcCaption: The prototype turned ideas into concrete screens.
props.settleLine: Now there's a clear interface to build against.

beats.narration_text: The prototype also made the bigger picture clearer. Once the core annotation tool works, the plan is to expand into full video processing, metadata extraction, automatic dataset generation, and eventually AI-assisted annotation that speeds up labeling before we get to actual loon detection.

show.event: A chip grid lists what comes after the core tool works.

props.caption: The core tool comes first; this is what it unlocks next.

beats.narration_text: So the honest state is this: we do not have a functional annotation tool yet, only a prototype and a clear plan. But real groundwork is done. The workflow is designed end to end, the interface is prototyped, and the repository is ready for real development to begin.

show.event: A verdict artifact summarizes the honest state of the project.

artifactLines: Moved from idea to a concrete workflow and a working prototype.
The annotation tool is prototyped, not yet functional.
The repository is set up as the foundation for real development.

beats.narration_text: Next week, I'm moving from the prototype into actual development: displaying frames, drawing bounding boxes, assigning the Loon label, and saving those annotations. If you want to help, start with one question: what's the simplest way to store a bounding-box annotation so it's easy to export later?

beats.narration_text: That is the update for this week. Thank you for watching, and I will see you next week.
